chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān and Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man takes from date-palms and crops before they are cut and harvested, then there is no amputation upon him. But when the date-palms have been cut and he takes, and the crop has been harvested and he takes, his hand is amputated.

key_terms.النَّخْلِ: date-palms from which dates are taken
key_terms.حُصِدَ: was harvested, said of the crop
key_terms.صُرِمَ: was cut or collected from the date-palms
key_terms.قَطْعٌ: amputation as the legal hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.يُصْرَمَ: to be cut from the trees or gathered

ai.seo_question: When does the hadd punishment apply to stealing dates or crops according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft from produce in the field or on the trees. It distinguishes between taking before harvest, for which the hadd punishment does not apply, and taking after harvesting or cutting, when the prescribed punishment for theft applies.
